# Troubleshooting

Exit codes, the errors you will actually meet, and the wire gotchas that
look like bugs but are protocol behavior.

## Exit codes

| Situation                     | Output              | Code |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------- | ---- |
| Bare invocation / bare group  | Help on stdout      | 0    |
| Leaf success                  | JSON on stdout      | 0    |
| Runtime / BRP error           | Message on stderr   | 1    |
| clap usage error (bad flags)  | Usage on stderr     | 2    |
| Watch stop conditions         | JSONL so far        | 0    |

Note: `status` exits 0 even when the app is down — reachability is data
(`reachable: false`), not a process error.

## Common errors

- **Connection refused / timed out** — the app is not running, not built
  with `RemotePlugin` + `RemoteHttpPlugin`, or on a different port. Run
  `bevy_copilot status` and check `reachable` / `probe_error`; fix with
  `--port` or `BEVY_BRP_PORT`. Timeouts: 2 s connect, 10 s ordinary request, 30 s screenshot; recording
  gets its duration plus 35 s.
- **`brp extras *` fails naming `bevy_copilot_extras`** — the app runs core
  BRP only. These calls self-gate on `rpc.discover` and refuse before
  POSTing. Add `BrpExtrasPlugin` to the app; everything non-extras keeps
  working meanwhile.
- **`brp rpc execute` refuses an unadvertised method** — same gate. Run
  `brp rpc discover` and pick a method from the list; apps expose custom
  verbs by registering them (e.g. `my_game/reset_level`).
- **Unknown / empty component type** — the type path is wrong or the type
  is not reflect-registered. List what exists with
  `brp world list-components` / `brp world list-resources` /
  `brp registry schema`, and have the app call `.register_type::<T>()`.
- **`invalid JSON: ...` before any network call** — shell quoting ate the
  payload. Single-quote JSON flags: `--data '{"components": [...]}'`.
- **clap usage error, exit 2** — wrong flag spelling or a bad enum value
  (e.g. `brp debug record --action`); the stderr usage text lists the valid
  values.
- **Mutation rejected by reflection** — wrong JSON shape, unsupported numeric
  conversion/range, or a missing intermediate field in
  `--path`. Check the field layout in `brp registry schema`.

## Wire gotchas (not bugs)

- **NaN / infinite floats arrive as `null`** — JSON cannot represent them,
  so Bevy's reflection serializer emits null. The `nan_transform` anomaly
  rule detects exactly this but cannot tell NaN from inf or a genuine null.
- **Entity ids are remapped by replay / checkpoint restore** — both spawn
  fresh entities and return `{applied, remapped, entity_map}`. Existing
  entities are not removed by restore; their IDs can remain valid. Replay maps only known method envelope fields and explicit
  journal `entity_paths` JSON pointers into params. Payload field names are not
  type information. Checkpoint restore does not rewrite payload references.
- **Only reflect-registered components survive** replay/restore, and a
  checkpoint only stores the components you captured with (default:
  Transform). Resources, hierarchy, and unregistered types are not captured.
- **Side effects are immediate** — spawn/insert/mutate/remove/despawn and
  extras input calls change the live app at once. No undo except
  `brp debug experiment` sessions.

## Experiment recovery and input routing

Experiment capture failures reject before writing. Mutation undo replaces the
entire captured component, so perform experiments in a controlled world: unrelated
live changes to that component would also be overwritten. Reflected components
must support reconstruction; hooks and arbitrary side effects are not reversible.
After any failed/interrupted write, inspect the live world and call
`brp_debug_experiment` with `{"action":"reset"}` before more experiment writes.
This deliberately clears local history; it does not undo remote work.

Synthetic keyboard input needs exactly one primary window. It carries that
window and named logical modifiers through press/release. A removed window cancels
queued typing without sending it to a replacement. Physical key text uses a US
layout; `type-text` reports unmappable characters as skipped, not IME input.

## Large results spill to disk

Any result over 64 KiB is written to `<state dir>/brp_spill_*.json` and
stdout gets `{"spilled": true, "path", "bytes", "preview"}` instead of the
payload. Read the spill file for the full document. Typical triggers:
`brp registry schema` and wide `world.query` calls — narrow them
(`--with-crates`, `--type-limit`, tighter `--data`).

## Watches that never end

`brp watch *` streams until a stop condition. Always pass `--frames <N>`
and/or `--max-ms <MS>`; all stop conditions (frame count, deadline, stream
end, closed downstream pipe, Ctrl-C) exit 0 — a deadline is not an error.
The 60 s budget ceiling applies to the MCP watch tools only, not the CLI.

## Debug state does not persist across CLI calls

Every CLI invocation starts with fresh in-process debug state:

- `brp debug record --action start` begins a journal that dies with the
  process — a later `stop` fails with `no recording in progress`;
- `brp debug observe` always diffs against an empty baseline;
- `brp debug experiment --action undo` has nothing recorded to undo;
- `brp debug replay` always replays `<state dir>/journal.jsonl`.

For session work (record across calls, incremental diffs, undo/redo) run
`bevy_copilot mcp` and use the `brp_debug_*` tools — that state lives for
the server's lifetime. What DOES persist across CLI calls: the saved
journal and named checkpoints, both under the state dir, so the surfaces
hand off cleanly.

## State dir and environment

The state dir is `<temp dir>/.bevy_copilot` (its exact path is in the
`status` output) and holds `journal.jsonl`, `checkpoints/<name>.json`, and
`brp_spill_*.json`. Environment overrides: `BEVY_BRP_HOST` (default
`127.0.0.1`), `BEVY_BRP_PORT` (default `15702`); precedence is
flags > env vars > defaults.

## MCP execution errors

A failed BRP operation returns an MCP tool result with `isError: true` and
`structuredContent: {code, message, data}`; its text block carries the same JSON.
Remote details such as camera candidates remain in `data`. Unknown tools and
malformed MCP requests remain protocol errors. CLI failures still exit 1 and
print diagnostics, including remote error data, on stderr.

For independent peers or sessions, give each process a private `TMPDIR`. The
same directory must be retained when handing a saved journal/checkpoint to a
later CLI process; selecting a different `--port` does not isolate state files.
